corrections.form_value: Two controlled online experiments compared Prolific participants working under different LLM support arrangements: the math study analyzed 315 people under no-agent, peers-only, tutor-only, or tutor-plus-peers support, and the writing study analyzed 247 people under no AI, a single generalist assistant, or two role-specialized assistants (PDF pp. 3–6 and 8). Math performance was tested after assistance was removed; writing outcomes were GPT-5.2-rated quality of creative and argumentative essays and semantic similarity of ideas across writers (PDF pp. 4 and 6–8). The paper does not state how participants entered the main support conditions; its explicit randomization statements concern topics, prompts, essay order, model identity within Single, and model roles within Duo, so the main contrasts cannot be classified as confirmed randomized or confirmed non-randomized comparisons (PDF pp. 3–6).

Creative dimensions are originality, narrative structure/coherence, elaboration/richness, expressiveness/emotional impact, and literary quality/language use; argumentative dimensions are argument clarity, evidence/reasoning, logical structure/organization, counterarguments, persuasiveness, and language/formality. corrections.source_says: Fill the required diversity details: gpt-5-mini extracts 3–5 atomic key points per essay; SBERT embeds them (specific checkpoint not stated). The metric is mean pairwise cosine similarity among all key points within each condition × prompt cell, aggregated over prompts within condition. Resample 15 essays with replacement per cell for 1,000 bootstrap rounds to obtain means and 95% confidence intervals; pairwise tests shuffle essay condition labels for 1,000 permutation rounds and compare absolute difference magnitudes. Figure 7 instead labels its error bars ±1 SEM. Higher similarity means lower diversity; these are set-level results, not independent-person counts.
corrections.quote: We embed each key point using a sentence transformer (SBERT) and compute the mean pairwise cosine similarity among all key points within each (condition × prompt) cell.
corrections.locator: Main PDF p. 7, section 4.1.4 and Figure 7 caption; p. 8, section 4.2.2.

confirmed: Read the entire local markdown and all 12 PDF pages, including references; the document is arXiv:2604.02677v2 dated 3 July 2026 and labeled Working Paper, July 2026 (PDF p. 1 version stamp; p. 2 header; final references on p. 12).
The title and four named authors in the form match the title page (PDF p. 1). The system-prompt Appendix is referenced but absent from this PDF (p. 2, section 3.1.1; document ends on p. 12).

The checker additionally read both linked preregistrations as public HTML and complete PDFs in memory: rq8uz9, 2 pages, preregistered 2026-02-04; gq922f, 1 page, preregistered 2026-02-16 (registration headers; links in main PDF pp. 2 and 5).

S1 recruited 614 people and analyzed 315 who passed checks; S2 recruited 419 people and analyzed 247 who produced two usable essays. These are people, not essays, key points, ratings, or pair counts, and both analyzed samples exceed 50 (PDF p. 4, section 3.1.5; p. 8, section 4.1.5).
The abstract reports 562 participants across the two experiments, not 562 writers (PDF p. 1, Abstract; study-specific counts on pp. 4 and 8).

Actual numbers randomized and analyzed counts per arm are not reported, so the form correctly leaves these null. The writing protocol's planned 360 participants, approximately 120 per condition, are recruitment targets rather than observed counts (main PDF pp. 4–8; AsPredicted gq922f PDF p. 1, question 7).

S1 uses SAT-level mathematics and an unassisted correctness test rather than creativity or diversity scoring; its exclusion from creativity-task scope is appropriate despite the randomized design (PDF p. 4, sections 3.1.3–3.1.4).

S2 combines a creative and an argumentative essay per participant; GPT-5.2 rubric ratings yield participant-level combined quality, while key-point similarity summarizes condition-level pools. The construct/question/measure/unit classifications usefulness/with_ai/automated_score/participant and diversity/across_people/embedding_similarity/set are supported (PDF pp. 6–8, sections 4.1.3–4.2.2).

The first reported string is numerically exact: Control vs. Single, Δ=0.332, t(244)=6.21, p<.0001, with Bonferroni correction and Single higher; combined quality is reported on a 1–5 scale (PDF p. 8, section 4.2.1; p. 7, Figure 7a).

The one-line finding correctly gives the additional Control vs. Duo quality difference Δ=0.234. The paper also reports t(244)=4.21, p=0.0001, and Single vs. Duo Δ=0.098, t(244)=1.56, p=0.363 (PDF p. 8, section 4.2.1).

The second reported string and the one-line finding correctly give Duo similarity 0.737, Single 0.748, and Duo vs. Single permutation p=.065; higher similarity means greater homogenization. The same passage reports Control 0.735, Single vs. Control p=.033, and Duo vs. Control p=.950 (PDF p. 8, section 4.2.2).

The human-validation subset comprises 83 essays (49 creative, 34 argumentative) scored by two raters, not an alternative participant sample; the form correctly uses the full analyzed participant count instead (PDF p. 7, section 4.1.4).

The models and roles are correctly described: GPT-5.2 for the math agents; Claude Opus 4.6 or GPT-5.2 in Single, and both models with complementary roles in Duo (PDF p. 2, section 3.1.1; pp. 5–6, section 4.1.2).

Task duration details match: math approximately 14 minutes, 5-minute supported lessons, and a 1-minute Tetris interval; writing approximately 200–300 words per essay and median 11-minute completion. The form correctly preserves the paper's conflict between at least 5 minutes and a 5-minute limit per essay (PDF p. 4, sections 3.1.4–3.1.5; p. 5, section 4.1.1; p. 6, section 4.1.3; p. 8, section 4.1.5).

This is primary experimental research, not a synthesis or AI-only versus human-output comparison; leaving synthesis counts/pooled estimates empty and context_class=none is appropriate (PDF pp. 2–8, sections 3–4; codebook sections 3–4).
summary: The linked preregistrations document random assignment to the main conditions, so the writing study with 247 analyzed participants qualifies for the two-screener pipeline. The recorded sample counts and result statistics match the PDF, but design and eligibility, preregistration, source-access notes, and omitted outcome details require correction.
